title: Implement and Integrate a New 'Corporate Conference' Analytics Strategy
description: The 'Backstage Pulse' ETL system is being expanded to support a new market: corporate conferences. This requires a new data processing strategy to handle events specific to this domain, such as attendee engagement and lead capture. This task is divided into three distinct development sessions, simulating a realistic workflow where a developer builds, integrates, and finalizes a feature over several days. The agent must retain context between sessions to successfully complete the project.

project_spec.name: Backstage Pulse – Real-Time ETL for Live Show Analytics
project_spec.description:
Backstage Pulse (Project ID: c_data_etl_medium_083) turns the raw telemetry generated by concerts, e-sports tournaments, and theme-park attractions into actionable intelligence for producers, light-board operators, and merchandising teams. Edge devices—lighting rigs, game servers, ticket scanners, concession PoS terminals—stream unstructured events (e.g., “laser_color_change”, “player_killstreak”, “popcorn_sale”) to the system. An event-streaming core fan-outs each message through an ETL pipeline written in C, applying Strategy-pattern plug-ins that transform payloads depending on show type (concert, e-sport, ride). Cleaned data is persisted into a tiered Data Lake (hot Redis cache → Parquet files in S3-compatible object storage), while nightly batch jobs summarize revenue, crowd heat-maps, and latency metrics for visualization.

The platform offers a WebSocket monitoring dashboard showing real-time KPI widgets—crowd energy score, merch velocity, network jitter—driven by aggregated event streams. Built-in data-quality checks flag outliers (e.g., impossible seat numbers, negative prices), while a scheduling module orchestrates batch replays and schema validations before every performance. Because everything from pyrotechnic timings to dynamic ticket repricing depends on fresh insights, the event-driven architecture guarantees low-latency fan-out and easy insertion of new entertainment-specific processors (e.g., “confetti_cannon_predictor”) without halting the show.
dependencies: librdkafka (C/C++ Apache Kafka client for event streaming)
SQLite/SQLite3 (local staging storage; embeddable in C)
GTK4 or Dear ImGui (optional native visualization front-end)
OpenSSL (secure TLS connectivity to brokers and dashboards)
